# dlarra

> Computes the splitting points with threshold based on the representation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlarra from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarra';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlarra(
    N,
    d, strideD,
    e, strideE,
    E2, strideE2,
    spltol, tnrm,
    nsplit,
    ISPLIT, strideISPLIT
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix, length N |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Subdiagonal elements (in/out), length N |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Squares of subdiagonal elements (in/out), length N |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | Stride length for `E2` |
| `spltol` | `number` | Splitting threshold |
| `tnrm` | `number` | Norm of the matrix |
| `nsplit` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output: number of blocks (nsplit[0]) |
| `ISPLIT` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: splitting points array |
| ↳ `strideISPLIT` | `integer` | Stride length for `ISPLIT` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N > 0$.
- `d`: On entry, the N diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: On entry, the first (N-1) entries contain the subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; `E(N)` need not be set. On exit, the entries E( ISPLIT( I ) ), $1 \le I \le \mathrm{NSPLIT}$, are set to zero, the other entries of E are untouched.
- `E2`: On entry, the first (N-1) entries contain the SQUARES of the subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; `E2(N)` need not be set. On exit, the entries E2( ISPLIT( I ) ), $1 \le I \le \mathrm{NSPLIT}$, have been set to zero
- `spltol`: The threshold for splitting. Two criteria can be used: $\mathrm{SPLTOL}<0$ : criterion based on absolute off-diagonal value $\mathrm{SPLTOL}>0$ : criterion that preserves relative accuracy
- `tnrm`: The norm of the matrix.
- `nsplit`: The number of blocks T splits into. $1 \le \mathrm{NSPLIT} \le N$.
- `ISPLIT`: The splitting points, at which T breaks up into blocks. The first block consists of rows/columns 1 to `ISPLIT(1)`, the second of rows/columns `ISPLIT(1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(2)`, etc., and the `NSPLIT`-th consists of rows/columns `ISPLIT(NSPLIT-1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(NSPLIT)=N`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: status code (0 = success)

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlarra.strided(
    N,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    e, strideE, offsetE,
    E2, strideE2, offsetE2,
    spltol, tnrm,
    nsplit,
    ISPLIT, strideISPLIT, offsetISPLIT
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix, length N |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Subdiagonal elements (in/out), length N |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |
| `E2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Squares of subdiagonal elements (in/out), length N |
| ↳ `strideE2` | `integer` | Stride length for `E2` |
| ↳ `offsetE2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `E2` |
| `spltol` | `number` | Splitting threshold |
| `tnrm` | `number` | Norm of the matrix |
| `nsplit` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output: number of blocks (nsplit[0]) |
| `ISPLIT` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: splitting points array |
| ↳ `strideISPLIT` | `integer` | Stride length for `ISPLIT` |
| ↳ `offsetISPLIT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `ISPLIT` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N > 0$.
- `d`: On entry, the N diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T.
- `e`: On entry, the first (N-1) entries contain the subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; `E(N)` need not be set. On exit, the entries E( ISPLIT( I ) ), $1 \le I \le \mathrm{NSPLIT}$, are set to zero, the other entries of E are untouched.
- `E2`: On entry, the first (N-1) entries contain the SQUARES of the subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix T; `E2(N)` need not be set. On exit, the entries E2( ISPLIT( I ) ), $1 \le I \le \mathrm{NSPLIT}$, have been set to zero
- `spltol`: The threshold for splitting. Two criteria can be used: $\mathrm{SPLTOL}<0$ : criterion based on absolute off-diagonal value $\mathrm{SPLTOL}>0$ : criterion that preserves relative accuracy
- `tnrm`: The norm of the matrix.
- `nsplit`: The number of blocks T splits into. $1 \le \mathrm{NSPLIT} \le N$.
- `ISPLIT`: The splitting points, at which T breaks up into blocks. The first block consists of rows/columns 1 to `ISPLIT(1)`, the second of rows/columns `ISPLIT(1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(2)`, etc., and the `NSPLIT`-th consists of rows/columns `ISPLIT(NSPLIT-1)`+1 through `ISPLIT(NSPLIT)=N`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: status code (0 = success)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlarra()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLARRA`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlarra.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlarra from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlarra';

// Symmetric tridiagonal matrix with a negligible off-diagonal entry:
var N = 4;
var d = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.0 ] );
var e = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0e-20, 0.5, 0.0 ] );
var E2 = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0e-40, 0.25, 0.0 ] );
var nsplit = new Int32Array( 1 );
var ISPLIT = new Int32Array( N );

// Using the standard interface (absolute splitting criterion):
var info = dlarra( N, d, 1, e, 1, E2, 1, -1.0e-10, 5.0, nsplit, ISPLIT, 1 );
console.log( info, nsplit, ISPLIT ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the strided interface:
info = dlarra.strided( N, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0, E2, 1, 0, -1.0e-10, 5.0, nsplit, ISPLIT, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, nsplit, ISPLIT ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>
